text: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice tells its story mainly through direct character dialogue rather than hidden item descriptions, making it clearer than Bloodborne or Dark Souls.
Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by FromSoftware.

The game was published internationally by Activision and in Japan by FromSoftware itself for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One in March 2019, with a Stadia version following in October 2020; Cube Game published in the Asia-Pacific region.
Hidetaka Miyazaki wanted to create a new intellectual property distinct from Dark Souls, aiming for a Japanese-themed game centered on shinobi and ninja.
The Tenchu series, tied to FromSoftware's history with historical Japanese settings, served as the impetus for Sekiro's development.
Development of Sekiro began in late 2015, following completion of Bloodborne's downloadable content, The Old Hunters.
Sekiro was directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, who had previously worked on the Dark Souls series and Bloodborne.

Sekiro draws inspiration from the Tenchu series of stealth-action games developed by Acquire and published by FromSoftware; the development team initially considered making Sekiro a sequel to Tenchu, but the concept outgrew that idea.
Miyazaki wanted the combat redesign to evoke the feeling of swords clashing, with fighters seeking openings for a fatal strike.
Miyazaki and the development team made Sekiro an entirely single-player experience because they felt multiplayer had limitations they wanted to avoid.

Sekiro was revealed via a teaser trailer at The Game Awards 2017 with the tagline 'Shadows Die Twice,' and the full title Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice was revealed during Microsoft's E3 2018 press conference.
The game's soundtrack was composed by Yuka Kitamura, with contributions from Noriyuki Asakura.
Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice was released for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One on 22 March 2019.
A collector's edition released the same day included a steelbook case, a figurine of the protagonist, an art book, a physical map, a soundtrack download code, and in-game coin replicas.
A Stadia port of Sekiro was released in late 2020.
On 31 October 2020, a free update added new content including new cosmetics for Wolf and a boss rush mode.
The word 'sekirō' is a contraction of 'sekiwan no ōkami,' meaning 'one-armed wolf.'
The subtitle 'Shadows Die Twice' was originally meant only as a teaser trailer slogan until Activision asked to keep it as part of the final title.
Sekiro received critical acclaim and was praised for its gameplay and setting, often compared favorably to FromSoftware's earlier work, though its difficulty drew mixed reactions.
Sekiro won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2019.
As of September 2023, Sekiro has sold over 10 million units.
On release day, Sekiro drew over 108,000 concurrent players on Steam, the highest for a new game launched in early 2019 and third highest for any Japanese game in Steam's history at the time.
In Japan, Sekiro sold 157,548 retail units in its opening weekend, debuting at number one.
Within ten days of release, Sekiro sold over two million units, rising to over five million units by July 2020.
An anime adaptation titled Sekiro: No Defeat was announced at Gamescom 2025, produced by Qzil.la, set to premiere in January 2027 for eight episodes, streaming on Crunchyroll outside Japan.
The anime's main cast reprises the voice roles of Daisuke Namikawa as Wolf, Miyuki Satou as Kuro, and Kenjiro Tsuda as Genichiro Ashina.
A theatrical edition of the Sekiro: No Defeat anime opened in Japanese theaters on 4 September 2026, distributed by Animec.
